elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and confirms that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 is phrased as a permission rather than a prohibition.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to one specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction is imposed at all, so the condition for limiting an imposed restriction to a named product is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the agreement term.
elements.evidence: No restriction applies during or after the term. The twenty-four-month language in Section 12.4 qualifies an express permission, not a prohibition.

elements.element: Any restriction lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: There is no restrictive period. Section 12.4's twenty-four-month period applies only to permissive language, while Section 12.3 provides an unqualified right to compete.

elements.element: Customer's internal development is carved out from any restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service, and Section 12.4 also permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Customer's acquisitions are carved out from any restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service, and Section 12.4 also permits acquisition of competing products or services.

result.reason: The operative text achieves the preferred position by eliminating the prohibition and retaining Section 12.3's comprehensive statement that Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction. It therefore also substantively exceeds the fallback protections. The edit is narrow and does not alter unrelated commercial obligations. However, drafting quality is poor because Section 12.4 retains an unnecessary twenty-four-month temporal qualifier on a permission, creating avoidable ambiguity about whether that permission is limited despite Section 12.3's broader language.
